delete_asset on '/Game/MyGame/Map/MainMap': that logical path is a MAP (class: World), not an ordinary asset. This call starts deleting the MAP and everything that hangs from it (for a World Partition map, every external actor package that references it). Cancelling the request on the client does NOT stop it: the command keeps running inside the editor, and only killing the process stops it. THE TRAP: if what you meant to delete was the stray `.uasset` the editor can write next to a read-only `.umap` (e.g. a .umap locked by Git LFS), both share the same name and differ only by extension -- which this path does not carry. WHAT WORKS, as an exception to the usual rule: for that stray file, close the editor and delete the file from disk. For the real map there is no way from here: it is not deleted.

subscribe_to_delegate('OnTakeAnyDamage' on BP_X_0): could NOT confirm that this delegate is declared by a Blueprint, and without that confirmation the call is not sent. import unreal
sds = unreal.get_editor_subsystem(unreal.SubobjectDataSubsystem)
sds.delete_subobject(ctx, dead)
sds.rename_subobject(alive, 'CollisionShell')

expect.message: execute_python: this script calls both delete_subobject AND rename_subobject. That sequence CRASHES THE EDITOR (fatal in Obj.cpp: 'Renaming on top of an existing object is not allowed') and cannot return an error. The trap is not renaming onto a taken name: the name is FREE in the Blueprint but still TAKEN in the instance ALREADY PLACED in the level, because delete_subobject removes the component from the SCS but does not reach what that instance serialized. RULE: do not rename an SCS component -- if the name matters, create it with the right name, and if it already exists under another name, adapt whatever reads it. WHAT WORKS if it must be done anyway: delete -> compile_blueprint -> save_level -> re-read the instances with list_world_partition_actors -> rename, in SEPARATE CALLS, never both steps in the same script. WARNING: if the name ends in a digit you did not ask for (MyComponent1), Unreal made it unique because a namesake ALREADY exists: find out what it is instead of renaming over it.

execute_python: this script WRITES attribute_set_types (set_editor_property (positional)), and that CRASHES THE EDITOR inside the call: assertion in Array.h, 'Array index out of bounds: 1 into an array of size 1'. UMaterialExpressionSetMaterialAttributes keeps TWO parallel arrays (Inputs and AttributeSetTypes); writing AttributeSetTypes through reflection does NOT grow Inputs, and PostEditChangeProperty indexes Inputs[1]. There is no return, so there is no success:false to rely on: the process goes down with every unsaved material edit. The two arrays are only kept in sync by the node's '+' button in the Material Editor (manual work for the user). WHAT WORKS: use the Displacement pin of MakeMaterialAttributes, reachable by name -- there is no need to touch this node. READING the property IS allowed (get_editor_property returns [] without error); only writing it crashes.

execute_python: SkeletalMergingLibrary.merge_meshes CRASHES THE EDITOR with an assert, not an exception (Assertion failed: (Index >= 0) & (Index < ArrayNum), 'Array index out of bounds: 1 into an array of size 1', not an ensure). It indexes the parallel arrays mesh_section_mappings and uv_transforms_per_mesh by NUMBER OF MESHES without validating them, so with 2 meshes and those arrays empty it crashes and takes everything unsaved with it. With a SINGLE mesh it is harmless: the crash starts at TWO, which is exactly the useful case. IF YOU STILL NEED IT: fill EVERY parallel array to the size of meshes_to_merge before calling it. NOTE: re-skinning has no headless path in UE 5.8: Skeleton is read-only through reflection, no MCP tool assigns a skeleton, SkeletalMeshEditorSubsystem only exposes assign_physics_asset, and IKRetargetBatchOperation is for ANIMATIONS. The step that produces the mesh is done in the editor (right-click the SkeletalMesh -> Skeleton -> Assign Skeleton).

execute_python: TextureExporterPNG CRASHES THE EDITOR if the texture is not 8 bits per channel (Assertion failed: SupportsTexture(Texture), EditorFactories.cpp, not an ensure). With a texture from an RTF_RGBA16F render target, or TC_HDR, or TC_EDITOR_ICON over float data, there is no return value: there is an assert. And the rule is not 'check the bit depth', it is DO NOT EXPORT AN IMAGE TO LOOK AT IT: to verify a capture, COUNT PIXELS with unreal.RenderingLibrary.read_render_target_raw / read_render_target_uv. IF YOU REALLY NEED A FILE: export_render_target is the supported path, or create the texture from an RTF_RGBA8 render target.

execute_python: request_auto_rigging CRASHES THE EDITOR IMMEDIATELY (Assertion failed: IsValid(), SharedPointer.h, not an ensure; script stack MetaHumanCharacterEditorSubsystem.RequestAutoRigging), and it is not a local failure: METAHUMAN AUTO-RIGGING IS A CLOUD SERVICE. The observed chain: no Epic session -> EOS_InvalidAuth -> no autorig -> 'Character is not rigged' in the UI -> can_build_meta_human:false -> Assemble disabled. rig_type=JOINTS_ONLY makes no difference. It is not blocked because it is impossible, but because what decides it is the ACCOUNT STATE, which cannot be read from the code: if you believe there is an Epic session, check it FIRST with get_output_log_lines(category_filter='MetaHuman') WITHOUT a verbosity filter -- LogMetaHumanAuth logs at Display, not Error, so with a filter it does NOT show. And save EVERYTHING before any attempt: this is an assert, not an exception.
